newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. demands Israel halt building in E. Jerusalem.
newsitem.headline: U.N. demands Israel halt building in E. Jerusalem.

text.p: An emergency special session of the General Assembly on Friday demanded an immediate halt to the construction of an Israeli settlement in East Jerusalem.
A resolution passed by 134 votes to three, with 11 abstentions, also called for an end to all assistance to "illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories.
The negative votes were cast by the United States, Israel and Micronesia.

The special session, convened on Thursday, was the fourth debate by a U.N. body an Israel's decision last month to build 6,500 homes for Jews at a site between Jerusalem and Bethlehem called Har Homa in Hebrew and Jabal Abu Ghneim in Arabic.

The resolution "condemns the construction by Israel, the occupying power, of a new settlement in Jabal Abu Ghneim. It demanded "immediate and full cessation of the construction... and of all other Israeli settlement activities."

In an approach to sanctions, which only the Security Council can impose, the resolution called for "the cessation of all forms of assistance and support for illegal Israeli activities" in the occupied territories, particularly settlement activities.
